questions.question: Q4 What is the 'convoy effect' in FIFO scheduling?

answers.b: A large job blocking many smaller jobs behind it

explanations.b: Correct. One long job can cause all subsequent jobs to wait, regardless of their size.

questions.question: Q6 Which scheduling algorithm minimizes average wait time?

explanations.a: Incorrect. FIFO does not optimize for wait time.
explanations.c: Correct. SJF provably minimizes average waiting time.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This would maximize wait time.

answers.b: Computing cycles lost due to job evictions or restarts

explanations.b: Correct. When a job is killed without checkpointing, all its computational work is lost.

questions.question: Q8 What is GPU cluster utilization?

answers.a: The percentage of GPUs that are turned on
answers.b: The ratio of productive GPU time to total available GPU time
answers.c: The number of GPUs in the cluster

explanations.a: Incorrect. Turned on does not mean utilized.
explanations.b: Correct. Utilization measures how effectively GPU resources are being used for computation.

questions.question: Q9 Why does Fair-Share scheduling prevent starvation?

answers.b: It guarantees each user a proportional share of resources

explanations.b: Correct. Fair-Share ensures every user receives a minimum allocation, preventing indefinite waiting.

questions.question: Q10 What type of jobs benefit most from checkpointing?

answers.b: Long-running training jobs that take hours or days

explanations.a: Incorrect. Short jobs lose little progress if killed.
explanations.b: Correct. Long-running jobs lose significant work without checkpointing.
